+package yomikai.data.ai
+
+import org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertEquals
+import org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertTrue
+import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test
+
+/**
+ * Разбор вызовов инструментов.
+ *
+ * Скрин: модель писала канонический однострочный `@tool web_search {"query":"x"}`
+ * и получала в ответ «НЕ ВЫПОЛНЕНО: тот же вызов уже выполнялся в этом ходе».
+ * Причина была не в модели: каноническую строку находили ДВА парсера (по
+ * маркеру `@tool` и построчный), она попадала в список вызовов дважды, а цикл
+ * хода отдавал модели второй как повтор — про вызов, который как раз
+ * выполнился.
+ *
+ * Здесь проверяется чистое правило: одинаковые вызовы схлопываются по
+ * подписи, а порядок аргументов в JSON на подпись не влияет.
+ */
+class AiAgentToolCallParsingTest {
+
+    private val known = listOf("web_search", "web_fetch", "read_file", "turn_page")
+
+    private fun parse(text: String) = AiAgent.parseToolCallsIn(known, text)
+
+    @Test
+    fun `a canonical one-line call is parsed once`() {
+        val calls = parse("""@tool web_search {"query":"свалка"}""")
+        assertEquals(1, calls.size)
+        assertEquals("web_search", calls[0].name)
+        assertEquals("свалка", calls[0].args.optString("query"))
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun `a call without the tool keyword and without at is still parsed`() {
+        assertEquals(1, parse("""@web_fetch {"url":"https://example.com"}""").size)
+        assertEquals(1, parse("""read_file {"path":"a.txt"}""").size)
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun `a call in backticks is parsed`() {
+        val calls = parse("""сделаю так: `@tool turn_page {"to":"next"}`""")
+        assertEquals(1, calls.size)
+        assertEquals("turn_page", calls[0].name)
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun `a multiline call is parsed`() {
+        val calls = parse(
+            """
+            @tool web_fetch {
+              "url": "https://example.com/a",
+              "chars": 12000
+            }
+            """.trimIndent(),
+        )
+        assertEquals(1, calls.size)
+        assertEquals("https://example.com/a", calls[0].args.optString("url"))
+        assertEquals(12000, calls[0].args.optInt("chars"))
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun `an xml-style call is parsed`() {
+        val calls = parse(
+            "<tool_call>web_search<arg_key>query</arg_key><arg_value>сакура</arg_value></tool_call>",
+        )
+        assertEquals(1, calls.size)
+        assertEquals("web_search", calls[0].name)
+        assertEquals("сакура", calls[0].args.optString("query"))
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun `a call without arguments is parsed as an empty object`() {
+        val calls = parse("@tool turn_page")
+        assertEquals(1, calls.size)
+        assertTrue(calls[0].args.length() == 0)
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun `an unknown tool name is ignored`() {
+        assertTrue(parse("""@tool rm_rf_slash {}""").isEmpty())
+        // Имя известно, но аргументы не разобрались — вызова нет.
+        assertTrue(parse("""@tool web_search {это не json}""").isEmpty())
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun `different calls in one answer are all kept in order`() {
+        val calls = parse(
+            """
+            @tool web_search {"query":"раз"}
+            @tool web_search {"query":"два"}
+            """.trimIndent(),
+        )
+        assertEquals(listOf("раз", "два"), calls.map { it.args.optString("query") })
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun `the same call written twice is parsed once`() {
+        // Ровно тот случай из бага: два парсера нашли одну и ту же строку.
+        val calls = parse(
+            """
+            @tool web_search {"query":"раз"}
+            @tool web_search {"query":"раз"}
+            """.trimIndent(),
+        )
+        assertEquals(1, calls.size)
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun `argument order does not change the call identity`() {
+        val first = AiAgent.ToolCall(
+            "web_fetch",
+            org.json.JSONObject("""{"url":"https://a","chars":10}"""),
+        )
+        val second = AiAgent.ToolCall(
+            "web_fetch",
+            org.json.JSONObject("""{"chars":10,"url":"https://a"}"""),
+        )
+        assertEquals(AiAgent.callSignature(first), AiAgent.callSignature(second))
+    }
+}

+package yomikai.data.ai
+
+import io.kotest.matchers.shouldBe
+import io.kotest.matchers.string.shouldContain
+import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test
+
+/**
+ * Что агент показывает модели и что от неё прячет.
+ *
+ * Три правила, которые вытащили из реальных поломок:
+ *  • результат любого инструмента резался до 700 символов МОЛЧА — модель
+ *    считала, что файл прочитан целиком, и либо выдумывала вторую половину,
+ *    либо звала инструмент заново;
+ *  • файлы провайдеров из папки providers (там apiKey) читались агентом
+ *    дословно, а `plugin_create` с `kind=http` умеет отправить что угодно на
+ *    любой хост — вместе это давало утечку ключа по цепочке из прочитанной
+ *    страницы;
+ *  • блок знаний о книге уходил в каждый вызов целиком.
+ */
+class AiAgentToolOutputTest {
+
+    @Test
+    fun `a short result is passed through untouched`() {
+        AiAgent.toolOutputFor("read_file", "Город сегодня") shouldBe "read_file: Город сегодня"
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun `a long result is cut and says so`() {
+        val long = "я".repeat(50_000)
+        val shown = AiAgent.toolOutputFor("read_file", long)
+
+        shown.contains("обрезано") shouldBe true
+        shown.contains("из 50000 символов") shouldBe true
+        // Обрезка не должна раздувать вывод: бюджет 8000 плюс объявление.
+        (shown.length < 9_000) shouldBe true
+        shown.contains(long.take(7_900)) shouldBe true
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun `web results get a smaller budget than file reads`() {
+        val text = "я".repeat(50_000)
+        (AiAgent.toolOutputFor("web_fetch", text).length <
+            AiAgent.toolOutputFor("read_file", text).length) shouldBe true
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun `unknown tools still get a budget instead of a silent cut`() {
+        AiAgent.toolOutputFor("some_new_tool", "я".repeat(9_000)).contains("обрезано") shouldBe true
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun `provider files are closed for the agent`() {
+        AiAgent.secretGuard("providers/openrouter.json") shouldContain "ОТКАЗ"
+        AiAgent.secretGuard("./providers/x.json") shouldContain "ОТКАЗ"
+        // Папка с ключами может встретиться и вложенной.
+        AiAgent.secretGuard("books/providers/x.json") shouldContain "ОТКАЗ"
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun `ordinary workspace files stay readable`() {
+        AiAgent.secretGuard("books/1.json") shouldBe null
+        AiAgent.secretGuard("notes.md") shouldBe null
+        // Похожее имя, но это обычный файл, а не папка ключей.
+        AiAgent.secretGuard("providers.md") shouldBe null
+        AiAgent.secretGuard("books/providers.json") shouldBe null
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun `api keys are redacted from any text shown to the model`() {
+        val json = """{"id":"openrouter","baseUrl":"https://x","apiKey":"sk-or-v1-abcdef123456"}"""
+        val shown = AiAgent.redactSecrets(json)
+
+        shown.contains("sk-or-v1-abcdef123456") shouldBe false
+        shown.contains("скрыто агентом") shouldBe true
+        shown.contains("openrouter") shouldBe true
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun `redaction leaves ordinary json alone`() {
+        val json = """{"title":"Город","count":3}"""
+        AiAgent.redactSecrets(json) shouldBe json
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun `the book knowledge budget is bounded`() {
+        // Правило книги — до 6000 символов, правил бывает 120: без потолка блок
+        // знаний уезжал на десятки тысяч токенов в КАЖДЫЙ вызов модели.
+        BookKnowledge.MAX_RENDER_CHARS shouldBe 4_000
+        (BookKnowledge.MAX_RENDER_CHARS < 6_000) shouldBe true
+    }
+}

---

## B. Ranked improvement opportunities

Ranking is by **value / effort**. #1–#5 are cheap, high-yield. #6–#12 are structural. #13+ are cleanup.

---

### 1. `tuning()` is called inside the detector's per-pixel hot loops — 12 SharedPreferences reads × ~540 k pixels per pass
**`data/src/main/java/yomikai/data/ocr/CyrillicOcrEngine.kt:984`** and **`:1009`**
```kotlin
984:  if (visited[start] || probability[start] < tuning().detectorThreshold) continue
1009:  if (!visited[next] && probability[next] >= tuning().detectorThreshold) {
```
`tuning()` → `tuningProvider()` = `OcrRepositoryImpl::currentTuning` (`:66`) → `regionProfile()` (`:59-64`) → `tuningOverrides()` (`:80-89`) → **11 `.get()` calls on SharedPreferences + 3 object allocations** (`OcrRegionProfile`, `OcrTuningOverrides`, `OcrTuning` with 28 fields). `DETECTOR_SIZE²=541 696` (`:982`), so up to ~541 k calls in the outer loop plus up to ~8× that in the BFS neighbour loop (`:1003-1013`). With tiling (`:915-939`) that is ×5 passes → tens of millions of pref reads per page.

- **Why it matters:** This is very likely the dominant cost of local OCR and the direct cause of `OCR_FRAME_TIMEOUT_MS = 25_000` firings (`AutoReadEngine.kt:1602`) and "OCR frame timeout" history entries. The detector itself (736² conv) should be tens of ms; the pref reads dominate.
- **Fix:** Hoist `val t = tuning()` to the top of `runDetection` (and of `recognizeCrop`, `acceptsConfidence`, `lineBands`, `splitWords`, `detectTextBoxes`) — or memoize `regionProfile()` behind the prefs `.changes()` flow (there is already `Preference.changes()` in `AndroidPreference.kt:56`).
- **Impact:** **Speed — very large (likely 2–10× on local OCR), zero accuracy change.**
- **Regression risk:** **Very low.** Pure hoisting; semantics identical within one pass. (A stale-cache variant would introduce a settings-latency regression — prefer the plain hoist.)

---

### 2. `Regex(...)` is recompiled on every call inside per-crop cleanup/ranking
**`data/src/main/java/yomikai/data/ocr/OcrTextCleaner.kt`**
- `:185` `text.split(Regex("\\s+"))` in `isAcceptableCyrillicOcrText` — called 2–3× per crop (`CyrillicOcrEngine.kt:438, 900, 1238, 1253`)
- `:367` `text.split(Regex("[^\\p{L}\\p{N}]+"))` in `userDictionaryCoverage` — called from `candidateQuality` (`CyrillicOcrEngine.kt:1262`), ~4× per crop
- `:271, 275, 276` — **four** fresh `Regex` per `restoreKnownCaptionWords` call, which runs from `normalizeLocalCyrillicCaption` ← `needsWordSegmentation` (`:723`), `selectLineRecognition` (`:738`), `salvageRejectedLines` (`:435`), `cleanRecognition` (`:898`) → 2–3× per crop

Kotlin does **not** cache `Regex` literals; each `Regex("…")` is a fresh `Pattern.compile`. With ~128 boxes/page × ~6 calls × 3 patterns ≈ 2 300 pattern compilations per page.

- **Fix:** Promote to `private val` companions (`WHITESPACE`, `NON_LETTER`, `QUOTE_OPEN_AFTER_CAPS`, `PUNCT_BEFORE_CYRILLIC`, `WS_RUN`). `MangaTranslatorService.kt:19` already does this correctly.
- **Impact:** **Speed — moderate-to-large on page scan; zero accuracy change.**
- **Regression risk:** **Very low.**

---

### 3. `OcrRepositoryImpl.fallbackChain()` duplicates `OcrPlugins.fallbackChain()`, and silently drops OpenRouter + OwOCR
**`data/src/main/java/yomikai/data/ocr/OcrRepositoryImpl.kt:289-305`**
```kotlin
291: val online = listOf(EngineType.GLENS, EngineType.ZEN_FREE, EngineType.GOOGLE)
292:     .filter { onlineEngineReady(it) }
```
`OcrPlugins.fallbackChain()` (`OcrPlugins.kt:207-221`) is fully tested (`OcrPluginsTest.kt:210-236`) but **never called from production**. The runtime chain omits `OPENROUTER` and `OWOCR` entirely, so a user who configures an OpenRouter key or self-hosted OwOCR server never gets them as fallback — the exact "silent engine substitution" problem `OcrRepository.kt:26-34` was written to fix.

- **Fix:** make `OcrRepositoryImpl.fallbackChain` delegate to `OcrPlugins.fallbackChain` after mapping `EngineType → OcrPluginDescriptor` and filtering by `onlineEngineReady`.
- **Impact:** **Robustness/correctness — real**; **speed — positive** (chain gets longer, but only when actually configured).
- **Regression risk:** **Medium** — the chain order changes for `auto` (registry sorts by `fallbackPriority`: glens 10, zen 20, google 30, openrouter 40, owocr 50; the repo version has no sort). Gate behind a test comparing both chains.

---

### 4. Autoread/browser frames write garbage into the persistent OCR cache, and destroy the real bulk-scan result for the same page
- **`OcrRepositoryImpl.kt:580`** — `cacheStore.upsert(result)` is unconditional on every `scanPage`, including autoread viewport frames.
- **`BrowserTab.kt:1576` / `:1582`** — `chapterId = -1L`, `pageIndex = System.currentTimeMillis() % 1_000_000` → unbounded junk rows.
- **`BrowserTab.kt:750`** — `pageIndex = wv.scrollY` → one new page row per scroll step, chapter −1.
- **`BrowserTab.kt:1573` / `:1580`** — `prefsO.ocrModel().set(want)` **overwrites the user's global engine preference** as a side effect of a browser screenshot, permanently switching the reader to Google Lens or back to Cyrillic.

In webtoon, an autoread frame is a *viewport crop* of a segment, so `imageHeight` and every region box are relative to the frame. Upserting that under `(chapterId, pageIndex)` **overwrites the correct bulk-scan geometry** for that segment (`ocr_cache.sq:8` `UNIQUE(chapter_id,page_index,ocr_model) ON CONFLICT REPLACE`). `getCachedPage` then serves the wrong boxes to the reader overlay and to `ChapterOcrTranscript`.

- **Fix:** (a) add a `cacheResult: Boolean = true` / `source` discriminator to `scanPage` and pass `false` from `AutoReadEngine.readFrame` and `BrowserTab`; (b) pass the real engine to `recognizeText(image, model)` in `BrowserTab` instead of mutating prefs; (c) use `chapterId = 0`/`pageIndex = 0` sentinel and skip `upsert` there.
- **Impact:** **Accuracy (overlay boxes, transcripts) — high; speed — moderate** (removes a SQLite write transaction per frame from the speak loop); **robustness — high** (cache size bounded).
- **Regression risk:** **Low** if `cacheResult=false` is only applied to the autoread/browser call sites; run `OcrRepositoryImplTest` + `OcrScanManagerTest`.

---

### 5. Cache is never invalidated when the engine, preset, local mode, or tuning changes
`OcrCacheStore.kt:204-211` only invalidates on a manually-bumped `CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION = 2`. `getPage` (`ocr_cache.sq:33-38`) picks the newest row by `created_at`, so after the user switches `pref_ocr_content_type` BALANCED→MANGA, `pref_ocr_local_mode` accurate→fast, or any of the 8 `pref_ocr_*_override` fields, the reader keeps showing results produced under the old parameters. `getCachedChapterIds` (used for the "already scanned" badge) also reports stale chapters.

- **Fix:** derive a cache key/version from `(ocrModel, contentType, localMode, presetScanRegion, overrides…)` and store it in the page row; or simply call `ClearOcrCache` from `SettingsOcrScreen` whenever any OCR-affecting pref changes (they all use `.changes()`).
- **Impact:** **Accuracy — high** (this is a silent-wrong-results class bug, the same family as the OCR_INVESTIGATION regressions).
- **Regression risk:** **Medium** — nuking the cache on every preset tweak forces re-scan cost; prefer the version-column approach.

---

### 6. `mergeBoxes` is O(n³) with `removeAt`, and runs on the *raw* component set before `take(maxTextBoxes)`
**`CyrillicOcrEngine.kt:1117-1142`** — `while (changed) { for i … for j>i … { union; boxes.removeAt(j); restart outer } }`. Called at `:940` with **all** raw connected components, and `take(maxTextBoxes)` only happens at `:944`. When tiling triggers (`boxes.size < tilingMinTextBoxes`, `:915`) four extra detector passes are added first, so the raw set can reach several hundred boxes → up to 10⁷–10⁸ `Rect` operations plus O(n) `removeAt` per union. The same code path also runs inside `projectionBoxes` (`:1108`).

- **Fix:** cap the input list before merging (`boxes.sortedByDescending(area).take(maxTextBoxes * 3)`), and replace the restart-from-zero loop with a single pass + union-find / interval approach.
- **Impact:** **Speed — large on dense/low-contrast pages** (exactly the pages that trigger tiling).
- **Regression risk:** **Medium** — box merging geometry is what drives tap targets; the existing `OcrBoxGeometryTest` does not cover `mergeBoxes` at all, so add a characterisation test first.

---

### 7. Per-crop `IntArray(w*h)` allocations: up to 6 full-size arrays per box, 2 × full-page arrays in the rescue path
- `computeCropInkRatio` — **`CyrillicOcrEngine.kt:117-154`** allocates `pixels` + `gray` (`w*h` each) on **every** `recognizeCrop` call (`:1156`).
- `lineBands` — **`:582-630`** allocates `pixels` + `gray`.
- `splitWords` — **`:778-791`** allocates `pixels` + `gray`.
- `recognizeWholeImageFallback(image)` → `recognizeCrop(image)` → `computeCropInkRatio` on the **full page**: 2 × w·h × 4 B ≈ **20 MB for a 1600² frame** (`:457-461`).
- Plus `OcrRepositoryImpl.useBitmap` (`:1095-1106`) copies `IntArray → Bitmap` (native), and the caller already did `Bitmap → IntArray` (`OcrImageMapper.kt:8-13`, `AutoReadEngine.kt:336-340`). That's a full round-trip of two10 MB buffers per frame.

- **Fix:** reuse a single scratch `IntArray`/`gray` pair sized to a max (fields, like the existing `recognizerPixels`), or accumulate the ink-ratio histogram in one pass without materialising `gray`.
- **Impact:** **Speed + OOM robustness — high** (this is the likeliest source of the `OutOfMemoryError` branch at `ReaderViewModel.kt:1057`).
- **Regression risk:** **Low**, but the arrays are shared mutable state and must be guarded by the existing engine `mutex` (`:80`) — which is already held on every path.

---

### 8. Two clean bitmap leaks on the autoread hot path
- **`AutoReadEngine.kt:1396-1421`** `maskCircle()` returns a new ARGB bitmap; `ocrCroppedRegion` (`:1371`) only recycles `crop` in its `finally` (`:1376`), never `masked`. Up to `MAX_BUBBLES_PER_FRAME = 40` leaked native bitmaps per frame.
- **`AutoReadEngine.kt:1372`** allocates a fresh `IntArray` + `OcrImage` per bubble — unavoidable given the API, but the leak above is not.
- Also `maskCircle` builds a new `PorterDuffXfermode` and `Paint` per bubble and does two full pixel passes (`:1410-1419`); the erase oval is a *bounding* oval so any bubble outside 0.7–1.4 aspect never gets masked (`AutoReadEngine.kt:1246`).
- **`ReaderSelectionCropper.kt:134-146`** `clipToShape` also returns a new bitmap; the original is never recycled on the success path.

- **Fix:** recycle `masked`/`out` after `getText`; hoist the `Xfermode`/`Paint` to a field.
- **Impact:** **Robustness — high** (long autoread sessions eventually hit `OutOfMemoryError`); **speed — small**.
- **Regression risk:** **Low** (be careful not to recycle a bitmap still referenced by `OcrImage`).

---

### 9. No model preloading: first OCR call pays 3× `CompiledModel.create` + 2 dictionary reads *inside* the 25 s frame budget
`CyrillicOcrEngine.ensureInitialized()` (`:156-161`) → `init()` (`:163-209`) runs inside `mutex.withLock` on the repository's IO scope, triggered lazily from the first `recognizeText`/`recognizeLine`/`detectRegions`. `App.onCreate` (`app/src/main/java/yomikai/App.kt`) initialises `OcrVocabulary` (`:151`) and `OcrScreenshotBuffer` (`:157`) but never warms OCR. `OcrEvalRunner.kt:101-106` shows the authors know warmup is required ("иначе первая же цифра в отчёте была бы временем загрузки").

- **Fix:** `Application.onCreate` / `ReaderActivity.onCreate` → fire-and-forget `ocrRepository.warmUp()` that calls `engineFor(CYRILLIC).ensureInitialized()` (respecting `cyrillicModelsInstalled()`), and re-warm after `OcrModelDownloader` reports success.
- **Impact:** **Robustness (first-page latency, timeout) — high; speed — high for the first page.**
- **Regression risk:** **Low-medium** — adds ~50–100 MB peak RAM at app start on low-RAM devices; gate on `DeviceUtil.isLowRamDevice` and on the model pack being present.

---

### 10. `OcrStageBus` / `OcrTextCleanerStats` only observe `recognizeText`, so there is no observability of the dominant path
- `OcrStageBus.post` is called **only** from `CyrillicOcrEngine.detectRegions` (`:265`) and `recognizeText` (`:288, 290, 332, 335, 359, 368`).
- `scanPage` → `scanLocally` → `recognizeLine` (`:517`) posts **nothing**. So bulk scans, autoread frames, and every selection OCR produce no stage events, no `OcrStageBus` → reader spinner (`presentation/reader/components/ReaderFloatingControls.kt:140-142`) and **no `OcrHistoryStore.addScan` entries** (the history screen is therefore empty for exactly the flows users run most).
- `OcrTextCleanerStats.reset()` is called only at `CyrillicOcrEngine.kt:285` (inside `recognizeText`); the counters at `OcrTextCleaner.kt:267-269` and `:359` are non-atomic `+=` on `@Volatile Int` from a background thread → lost updates and meaningless counts on the `recognizeLine` path.

- **Fix:** move `reset()` + stage posting into a wrapper around the whole `scanPage` (or `OcrRepositoryImpl.scanLocally`); make the counters `AtomicInteger` or move them into a per-call context object.
- **Impact:** **Robustness (debuggability, user-visible honesty) — high; accuracy — indirect but high** (this is the instrumentation you need to validate items 1–9).
- **Regression risk:** **Very low.**

---

### 11. Panel/bubble detector `cleanup()` races with `getEngine()` and runs `CompiledModel.close()` on the main thread
**`data/src/main/java/yomikai/data/panel/PanelDetectionRepositoryImpl.kt:86-94`**
```kotlin
override fun cleanup() {
    engine?.close()      // no engineMutex, no inferenceMutex
    engine = null
```
Called from `App.onTrimMemory` (`App.kt:317-324`) and `ReaderViewModel.onCleared` (`:284-285`) — both main thread. `YoloPanelDetectionEngine.close()` (`:719-725`) calls `compiledModel.close()` synchronously (native) and recycles a shared `scratchBitmap` while `detectPanels` may be inside `inferenceMutex` writing to `inputFloatBuffer`/`outputBuffers`. Contrast with `OcrRepositoryImpl.closeEngines()` (`:1116-1152`), which correctly takes `engineLocks.withAllLocks`.

- **Fix:** take `engineMutex.withLock { inferenceMutex.withLock { … } }` (or `runBlocking` on IO like `CyrillicOcrEngine.close()` `:1414-1416`) and null out before closing.
- **Impact:** **Robustness — high** (native use-after-free / crash under memory pressure, exactly when autoread is most likely running). **Speed — none.**
- **Regression risk:** **Low**, but verify `cleanup()` doesn't now block the main thread for long.

---

### 12. Local engine is Cyrillic-only → Japanese/Korean/Chinese manga cannot be read offline at all
**`CyrillicOcrEngine.kt:1403-1412`**
```kotlin
return char in '\u0400'..'\u052F' || char.isWhitespace() || char in ALLOWED_PUNCTUATION
```
The CTC decoder *rejects every non-Cyrillic class*, so for a Japanese page `recognized` is empty → `rescueRejectedLines` (`:386`) → `recognizeWholeImageFallback` (`:457`) → `cleanRecognition` (`:894`) → `isAcceptableCyrillicOcrText` false → **empty string → "Нет результатов"**. Meanwhile `FastOcrEngine` / `LegacyOcrEngine` (manga-ocr, Japanese-capable, 515 + 365 lines of maintained code) are **unreachable**: `OcrRepositoryImpl.kt:212-213, 219` map `LEGACY`, `FAST`, `TESSERACT` → `EngineType.CYRILLIC`.

- **Fix (option A, cheap):** make `allowed()` script-aware off `pref_autoread_language` and remove the hard `isAcceptableCyrillicOcrText` gate when the language is not Cyrillic. **(option B):** restore `FAST`/`LEGACY` as selectable Japanese engines — they already exist, are wired in `engineFor` (`:330-339`) and downloadable via `OcrModelDownloader.PACKS["manga_ocr"]` (`:109-117`).
- **Impact:** **Accuracy — very large** for non-Cyrillic content; this app is a *manga* reader and the primary offline path cannot read manga.
- **Regression risk:** **Medium-high** for option A (releasing Latin classes reintroduces the "уверенный латинский мусор" regression documented at `OCR_INVESTIGATION.md:23` and `CyrillicOcrEngine.kt:1191-1195`). Option B is additive and lower-risk.

---

### 13. `EngineOptions` and the browser path silently rewrite the user's engine choice
- **`app/src/main/java/yomikai/ui/locallibrary/LocalOcrScreens.kt:167-188`** renders **all** `OcrModel.entries` (incl. `TESSERACT`, `LEGACY`, `FAST`) into the book / game / app engine pickers. `engineTypeOf()` (`OcrRepositoryImpl.kt:206-225`) then rewrites all three to `EngineType.CYRILLIC`. Picking "Tesseract" gives you PP-OCR.
- **`app/src/main/java/yomikai/data/books/BookOcr.kt:28`** calls `processor.getText(bmp.toOcrImage())` — it **ignores `pref_ocr_engine_book` entirely**, so `LocalOcrScreens.kt:465` has no effect on book OCR.
- **`OverlayAutoReader.kt:56,79`** honours `appOcrEngine()` but then funnels it through the same rewrite.

- **Fix:** drive the pickers from `OcrPlugins.ALL` (like `SettingsOcrPluginsScreen`) and either delete `LEGACY`/`FAST`/`TESSERACT` from `OcrModel` or wire them up; pass `bookOcrEngine()` into `BookOcr.recognize` as an explicit model.
- **Impact:** **Robustness/trust — high** (this is the same class of bug `OcrRepository.kt:26-34` documents: "на кнопке менялось только название").
- **Regression risk:** **Low** (mostly deletion of dead UI).

---

### 14. `isNetworkAvailable()` is a binder round-trip called up to 6× per page scan
**`OcrRepositoryImpl.kt:259-266`**, called at `:298`, `:419`, `:441`, `:642` — and `fallbackChain` itself (`:289`) re-reads `pref_fallback_preset` and re-checks readiness each time. It also has a latent NPE: `cm.activeNetwork` may be `null` and `getNetworkCapabilities(null)` is not allowed on all API levels (currently masked by `runCatching` at `:260`).

- **Fix:** cache with a short TTL (~5 s) or use `core/common`'s existing `NetworkState` / `activeNetworkState()` (already used in `OcrChapterScanner.kt:200`) which is flow-based.
- **Impact:** **Speed — small-to-moderate**; **robustness — small** (NPE masking).
- **Regression risk:** **Very low.**

---

### 15. `PrioritizedTaskQueue` HIGH priority does not preempt a running NORMAL item
`PrioritizedTaskQueue.kt:90-116`: `processQueue` takes one item, `scope.launch { … }`, then `job.join()`. Priority is only consulted *between* items. Because `scanLocally` submits one item **per box** (`OcrRepositoryImpl.kt:942-979`), a user-initiated `recognizeText` (HIGH, `:471`) does get picked up between boxes — good — but it still waits for the in-flight box, which is up to **4 recognizer passes** (`recognizeCrop` at `:1162-1220`: v3, v3+contrast, v5, v5+contrast) plus `lineBands` and possibly per-word passes.

- **Fix:** chunk a page scan into one queue item with internal `ensureActive()` checks (or reduce the granularity to N boxes), and cancel the in-flight box on a HIGH arrival.
- **Impact:** **Speed/interaction latency — moderate.**
- **Regression risk:** **Medium** (touches the cancellation semantics that `PrioritizedTaskQueueTest.kt` covers).

---

### 16. Row grouping is O(n²) with per-comparison re-allocation, and duplicated
**`CyrillicOcrEngine.kt:345-353`** and again at **`:397-405`** (`rescueRejectedLines`) — identical copy-pasted block:
```kotlin
val center = existing.map { it.first.centerY }.average().toFloat()
val height = existing.map { it.first.height }.average().toFloat()
```
Running `map{}.average()` on every candidate row for every item, and scanning `rows.firstOrNull` linearly. For 128 boxes that's ~8 k list allocations per page, twice.

- **Fix:** extract one `groupIntoRows()` helper keeping incremental sums; sort by `centerY` and use a single sweep (the pattern already used correctly in `AutoReadEngine.groupIntoBands`, `:1727-1742`).
- **Impact:** **Speed — small-to-moderate.**
- **Regression risk:** **Low** (behaviour-identical if incremental sums are exact — use running sums, not averages-of-averages).

---

### 17. Dead code that documents behaviour the code does not have
| Location | Problem |
|---|---|
| `OcrPlugins.kt:207-221` `fallbackChain()` | Never called in production (see #3) |
| `OcrTextCleaner.kt:385-398` `dictionaryCoverage()` | Never called. `OcrTuning.kt:246-252` documents the bonus as "встроенный `RuWordList` + пользовательский `OcrVocabulary`", but `candidateQuality` (`CyrillicOcrEngine.kt:1261-1262`) calls `userDictionaryCoverage`, which only consults `OcrVocabulary`. The built-in dictionary contributes **zero** to ranking. |
| `OcrTextCleaner.kt:461` `SMALL_WORDS` | Doc at `:460` says "им движок штрафует перерезанные куски"; nothing uses it |
| `Vocab.kt` (6 149 L), `FastVocabPart000/001.kt` (9 433 L), `FastVocab.kt` | ~15 600 lines of static vocab tables, no production reader found |
| `FastOcrEngine.kt`, `LegacyOcrEngine.kt` | 880 lines unreachable (see #12) |
| `OcrModel.TESSERACT` | No Tesseract code exists anywhere in the repo |
| `OcrPreferences.kt:90` comment | `//  offline   — только локальные (TESSERACT -> FAST -> LEGACY)` — describes a chain that no longer exists |
| `OcrPreferences.kt:211-229` | `tessLangs`, `tessPsm`, `tessUpscaleMinSide`, `tessPreprocess`, `keepOfflinePacks` — 5 orphan prefs, surfaced in `SettingsOcrScreen` |

- **Impact:** **Maintainability — high.** The `dictionaryCoverage` mismatch (#2 in this table) is a live accuracy bug, not just dead code.
- **Regression risk:** **Low** for deletions; **medium** for the `dictionaryCoverage` fix (changing ranking thresholds needs `OcrPluginsTest`/`OcrTextCleanerTest` re-run and a device CER check via `OcrEvalDialog`).

---

### 18. No automated accuracy gate; the CI "OCR quality report" contains zero measurements
- `.github/workflows/build.yml:57-59` runs **only** `OcrTextCleanerTest` as the "focused Cyrillic OCR regression tests" (the whole `./gradlew test` at `:63` does run everything, but nothing measures accuracy).
- `.github/workflows/release.yml:60` explicitly skips OCR/tests for release builds.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml:145-166` "Render OCR quality report" = a header table + `cat docs/ocr-releases/CURRENT.md`. `CURRENT.md` is hand-written prose about whichever feature shipped last (e.g. `docs/ocr-releases/2026-09-24-v1.9.97.md` documents *video generation through a GitHub runner*, not OCR).
- `OcrEvalRunner` (CER + detect/read timings over 6 synthetic variants) exists but is only reachable from `OcrEvalDialog` (`SettingsOcrScreen`) and its output is never committed.

- **Fix (highest leverage of anything on this list for *accuracy*):** (a) commit a small golden corpus (PNG crops + expected text) under `data/src/androidTest/assets/`; (b) run `OcrEvalRunner` from an `androidTest`/managed-device job and publish CER to the artifact; (c) at minimum, make `CURRENT.md` carry the measured CER table rather than prose.
- **Impact:** **Accuracy — enables everything else; robustness — prevents silent regressions** (which is how items #5, #12, #13 reached production).
- **Regression risk:** **Low** for (a)/(c); **medium** for (b) (managed-device minutes).

---

### 19. `OcrModelFiles.resolve()` does 6 filesystem `stat()`s per call, per model
**`data/src/main/java/yomikai/data/ocr/OcrModelFiles.kt:45-64`** — `resolve` builds up to 6 `File` candidates (`:48-61`) and each does `isFile && canRead() && length()`. `allInstalled` (`:67`) calls it per asset path, so `cyrillicModelsInstalled()` (`OcrRepositoryImpl.kt:382-391`) = 3 resolves = 18 stat() calls. `CyrillicOcrEngine.init()` (`:164-168`) does 5 more. `OcrPluginAvailability.availableIds()` (`:31-38`) repeats it for the settings screen. All of this runs on the IO thread but inside the frame budget.

- **Fix:** memoize the resolved base directory + a `Map<String, String?>` (invalidate on install/delete), and cache `allInstalled` behind the downloader callback.
- **Impact:** **Speed — small** (but trivially cheap to fix alongside #1).
- **Regression risk:** **Low**, but must invalidate on `OcrModelDownloader.downloadPack`/`deletePack`.

---

### 20. `OcrTextCleanerStats` / history double-counting, and `stripPromotionalText` recompiles two regexes per line
**`OcrTextCleaner.kt:97-98`** builds two `Regex` objects **per line** inside `stripPromotionalText`, which is called per region from `OcrRepositoryImpl.withoutPromotionalRegions()` (`:1035`), from `getCachedPage` (`:592`), and from `AutoReadEngine.cleanOcrGarbage` (`:1759`). Also `PROMOTIONAL_SITE`/`PROMOTIONAL_SLOGAN` are `Regex` fields (`:83, 87`) — good — but the `[ \t]{2,}` one at `:98` is not hoisted.

- **Fix:** hoist to a `private val`. Low risk, small win; fold into #2.

---

## C. "Known problems" grep results (verbatim)

There are **no `TODO`/`FIXME`/`XXX`/`HACK` markers in any OCR file**. The one relevant hit is adjacent:

- `app/src/main/java/yomikai/ui/reader/viewer/webtoon/WebtoonFrame.kt:15` — `* TODO consider integrating this class into [WebtoonViewer].`
- `app/src/main/java/yomikai/ui/reader/viewer/ReaderPageImageView.kt:95` — `// Reader-side workaround since image decoder doesn't display crop bounds:`
- `app/src/main/java/yomikai/presentation/more/settings/screen/SearchableSettings.kt:37` — `// HACK: for the background blipping thingy.`

The Russian-comment equivalents ("заглушка", "не работает", "временный", "известное ограничение") are all **resolved-regression narratives** rather than open bugs — e.g. `OcrRepositoryImpl.kt:369` ("Пока модели не скачаны … — заглушка"), `:887` ("Раньше заглушка бросала всегда"), `OcrNotificationManager.kt:74` ("Действия добавляются через PendingIntent в Activity — здесь заглушка для логгирования" — **this one is still open**: the notification's "Копировать"/"Озвучить" buttons are added with `null` `PendingIntent`s at `:77-78`, so they are dead taps), `OcrModelFiles.kt:18-20` ("Legacy manual folders (best effort, may be unreadable on Android 11+)").

The **actionable open-item list lives in `todo.md`** and is still largely unchecked — notably `todo.md:3-9`, `:14-16`, `:20-26`, `:39-40`, `:44-48`, and `:143-145`. `OCR_INVESTIGATION.md:23` records the last device-verified failure class (v3 ranking wrong on clean Cyrillic), and `docs/ocr-releases/CURRENT.md` ends with an explicit "Точность распознавания игровых шрифтов не проверена" caveat.

---

## D. Suggested execution order

| Batch | Items | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| **1 — pure speed, no behaviour change** | #1, #2, #19, #20, #16 | Hoisting + `val` precomputation. Single-file edits, all covered by existing tests. Expect the largest measurable win with the smallest blast radius. |
| **2 — correctness/observability** | #10, #4, #5, #3 | Makes results trustworthy and stoppable; #4 also removes DB writes from the speak loop. |
| **3 — allocation/OOM** | #7, #8, #9, #11 | Directly targets the `OutOfMemoryError` branch at `ReaderViewModel.kt:1057` and the frame timeouts. |
| **4 — capability** | #12 (option B first), #13 | Un-ships the Japanese path; stops lying UIs. |
| **5 — gate** | #18 | Only worth doing once 1–4 land; without it you cannot prove any of them helped. |
</task_result>
</task>

## (c) Ranked improvement opportunities

Ranking is by value/effort. Each item: location → why it matters → expected impact → regression risk.

---

### 1. `book_learn {"url":…}` throws the page away — every learned rule is fabricated, with false provenance
**`AiAgent.kt:1418-1449`** (`val fetched = BookLearning.sanitize(webFetch(url, 20_000))` at :1428; the result is used *only* for the error check at :1429, then discarded; `BookKnowledge.addSource` at :1436 records the URL).

The onboarding instruction the model is given (`AiAgent.kt:403-411`) says: `web_search → book_learn {"url":…} → выведи конкретные правила`. The model **never receives the page text**, yet `BookKnowledge.addSourceTo` (:242-248) writes "https://… — прочитано dd.MM.yyyy" into `book.sources`, and `renderRules` (:326) prints "(источник: <url>)" next to each rule. So the UI shows verified-looking provenance for rules the model invented.

Blast radius is not just chat: `AutoReadEngine.bookReadingOrder()` (`app/.../data/tts/AutoReadEngine.kt:265-273`) trusts `KIND_READING_ORDER` rules above the preset, and `bubblesOnly()` (:292-299) trusts `KIND_BUBBLE` — a hallucinated rule can flip RTL↔vertical or make auto-read speak only bubbles.

*Fix:* return the fetched text (or a bounded excerpt + a stable citation) in the `ToolResult.output`, and mark rules stored without a matching source as `author=web-source-unverified` instead of attributing the URL.
*Impact:* high — turns the whole "learn the book" feature from noise into signal; removes silent mis-ordering in TTS.
*Risk:* medium — the model sees a large tool output, so the 700-char truncation (item 2) must be fixed together or the excerpt is lost again.

---

### 2. Every tool result is truncated to 700 characters with no truncation marker
**`AiAgent.kt:633`** (`"${finalR.name}: ${finalR.output.take(700)}"`), also `:668`.

`read_many` is engineered for a 12 000-char budget (`AiWorkspaceSurvey.kt:26`), `workspace_list` for 6 000 (`:23`), `web_fetch` accepts up to 60 000 (`AiAgent.kt:1984`), `book_recall` can be huge — and the loop throws 98 % of it away. The model sees a silently truncated string and concludes it read the whole file; `read_many`'s "Бюджет чтения исчерпан" bookkeeping is invisible to it.

*Fix:* per-tool output budgets (e.g. 8–12 K for file reads, 4 K for web), an explicit `… [обрезано: показано X из Y]` marker, and route the *un*truncated text only through the budgeted follow-up assembly.
*Impact:* high — directly fixes multi-file work, book knowledge recall, and page reading; reduces the retry/loop churn caused by the model re-calling tools it "didn't see".
*Risk:* low-medium — larger prompts; keep the total bounded and watch the free-model context window.

---

### 3. Tool-loop memory is one round deep, and the full prompt is re-sent every round
**`AiAgent.kt:519` (12 rounds), `:635-646` (`followUp`), `:648-652` (`reliableChat(chat, prompt + "\n\n(вызовы выполнены приложением)\n" + followUp, …)`).**

Only the *latest* round's outputs are forwarded; round 1's results are dropped from round 2 onward. And each round re-sends the whole `prompt` — book knowledge (`:437`), shared memory, onboarding, attachments, history (`:449-452`) — plus the ~10.2 K-char / ~15 KB system prompt (`AiAgent.kt:184`, measured) and the capability block. So (a) multi-step tasks lose state, and (b) cost per turn scales as rounds × full context.

*Fix:* accumulate a rolling tool transcript (budgeted, newest-first with a summary of older steps) in a `MutableList<String>` passed to `reliableChat`, and send book knowledge/rules once (or as a cached prefix) rather than every round.
*Impact:* high for multi-step agent work; materially lowers tokens per turn.
*Risk:* medium — changing the prompt shape can shift tool-call formatting on small models; guard with the existing parser (it is intentionally lenient) and add a round-2 test.

---

### 4. Canonical single-line tool calls are parsed **twice**, and the model is told the tool "was not executed"
**`AiAgent.kt:761-798` (multiline/balanced-JSON parser) and `:801-813` (per-line parser), both feeding `out`, returned un-deduplicated at `:814`.**

For `@tool web_search {"query":"x"}` both parsers emit an identical `ToolCall`. The dedup loop (`:531-543`) keeps the first and files the second under `skipped += call to "тот же вызов уже выполнялся в этом ходе"`, which is then rendered to the model at `:640-645` as `НЕ ВЫПОЛНЕНО (не повторяй эти вызовы): web_search: тот же вызов уже выполнялся в этом ходе`. The model is thus actively misinformed about a call that *did* run — for the single most common formatting.

*Fix:* `parseToolCalls(...).distinctBy { callSignature(it) }` at the return site (the signature helper already exists at `:174` and is order-insensitive).
*Impact:* high — removes a per-call false negative in the feedback channel; small diff, big behavioural win.
*Risk:* very low. Add a `parseToolCalls` unit test (currently untested — see item 14).

---

### 5. Secrets live inside the agent's readable workspace and the tool set can exfiltrate them
**`AiProviders.kt:57-60` (`workspace/providers/<id>.json` containing `apiKey`, `:174-180` `toJson`), `AiAgent.kt:1563-1594` (`read_file` returns raw file text, no redaction), `AiPlugins.kt:154-173` (arbitrary HTTP method/headers/body to any host), `AiAgent.kt:1666-1677` (`zip_workspace` bundles providers + history).**

Chain: prompt-injected web text (from `web_fetch`) → model → `read_file providers/x.json` (returns the OpenRouter/custom key verbatim) → `plugin_create` with `kind=http`, `method=POST`, `body={apiKey}` → attacker host. Nothing in the loop requires confirmation, and `book_learn`/`book_recall` rules are re-injected as DATA on every future turn (`BookKnowledge.render` at `AiAgent.kt:437`), so the injection persists.

*Fix (layered, cheap first):* (a) deny `read_file`/`read_many` for `providers/`, `ui/`, `skills/`, `*.json` with a "перенастрой провайдера вручную" message; (b) redact `"apiKey"` in any file text returned to the model; (c) strip `apiKey` from `zip_workspace` or move it to EncryptedSharedPreferences/Keystore; (d) require an explicit user tap for `provider_*` / `plugin_create(http)` when the turn was triggered by fetched content.
*Impact:* high — this is the only realistic path from "read one manga wiki page" to "attacker owns the account's API key".
*Risk:* low for (a)/(b); medium for (d) (breaks the "just do it" UX the prompt advertises).

---

### 6. `AiHttpServer`: LAN-wide, CORS `*`, bearer token in the query string, no rate limit, no UI to manage it
**`AiHttpServer.kt:44` (`PORT = 8765`), `:66-68` (`bind(InetSocketAddress("0.0.0.0", PORT))`), `:71-84` (thread-per-connection, unbounded), `:98` (`soTimeout = 180_000`), `:128-136` (auth by `?key=`), `:142-150` (`POST /chat` → `runBlocking { AiAgent.run(context, text) }` — the **full** 63-tool agent, no `mangaId`, no `chatFn`, empty history), `:224-235` (`POST /ocr/settings` writes prefs), `:466` (`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` on every response, including `/file` bytes), `App.kt:94-101` (auto-start).**

Specifics: the token is in the URL so it lands in browser history/proxy logs; any page on the LAN can read `/files` and post to `/chat`; `runBlocking` can block a socket thread for 13+ minutes (`TOOL_TIMEOUT_MS["runner_start"] = 13 min`, `AiAgent.kt:123`) while the client socket dies at 180 s, leaving the agent still running. And the 401 help text (`AiHttpServer.kt:133`) tells the user to open "вкладка AI — блок «Доступ из внешнего браузера»" — **that UI does not exist** (I read all of `AiChatTab.kt`); the only control is the settings switch, so the feature is unusable-by-design and its recovery path is a dead end.

*Fix:* bind to loopback by default (opt-in to `0.0.0.0` with a visible warning), move the token to an `Authorization` header with a one-time pairing code, drop `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, cap concurrent requests, run `/chat` on a supervised scope with a turn deadline, and add a real "Внешний доступ" block in the AI tab showing the URL, the key, and start/stop.
*Impact:* high for security posture and for the feature actually being usable; medium for effort.
*Risk:* low for existing users (default was already off — `pref_ai_http_server` default `false`, `OcrPreferences.kt:241`).

---

### 7. AI-tab WebView hands the runner session key to any HTTP auth challenge, with JS + mixed content
**`AiChatTab.kt:318-395`**: `:334` `javaScriptEnabled = true`, `:340` `mixedContentMode = MIXED_CONTENT_ALWAYS_ALLOW`, `:342-349` `onReceivedHttpAuthRequest` → `handler.proceed("yomikai", session.apiKey.orEmpty())` **without checking `host`**, `:390` `loadUrl(url)` where `url` comes from a persisted JSON file (`RunnerLlm.Session.terminalUrl`, `RunnerLlm.kt:40-42`, persisted in `files/llm_sessions/*.json`).

Android invokes that callback for any host that challenges; the credential is the tunnel key, and on the runner that key fronts a hub whose `GH_TOKEN` gives write access to every repository of the account (`RunnerLlm.kt:746-747` states this explicitly, and `npm-hub/src/server.js` uses `process.env.GH_TOKEN` for arbitrary GitHub API calls).

*Fix:* compare `host` against the session URL's host before `proceed`; set `MIXED_CONTENT_NEVER_ALLOW`; disable `allowFileAccess`/`allowContentAccess`; only allow `https`.
*Impact:* high — closes a credential-disclosure path that a hostile or hijacked tunnel can exploit.
*Risk:* low-medium — if the tunnel ever serves over plain HTTP, the tunnel breaks (test on-device).

---

### 8. Latency/timeouts multiply far past any user expectation
**`AiAssistant.kt:508-509` (15 s connect, 90 s read) × `:391-430` rotation over up to 7 models × 3 transient retries × `:329-333` (`reliableChat` retries the whole call 3×, `AiAgent.kt:323-354`) × up to 12 rounds (`AiAgent.kt:519`).**

Worst case for one tool-free turn is many minutes with no streaming (`ZenProtocol.kt:144` `"stream", false`; no SSE anywhere) — the overlay shows a spinner and "AI думает" and nothing else. Additionally `withTimeoutOrNull` at `AiAgent.kt:600` cannot interrupt blocking `HttpURLConnection` reads, so a tool reported as "не ответил за …" can still finish writing files afterwards.

*Fix:* an overall per-turn deadline (`withTimeout`) surfaced honestly in the UI; SSE streaming for the online backend with partial rendering; make blocking HTTP calls cancellable (OkHttp/`Dispatchers.IO` + `invokeOnCancellation { conn.disconnect() }`) so tool timeouts actually stop work.
*Impact:* high for perceived quality; medium-high effort.
*Risk:* medium — streaming changes the response-parsing path (`ZenProtocol.parse`) and the `complete`/continuation logic that `reliableChat` depends on.

---

### 9. The token budget is enforced only on history, not on the knowledge blocks
**`AiAgent.kt:371-383` (budget/limit apply to `history` only), `:437` (`bookContext` prepended verbatim), `BookKnowledge.render()` (`:283-310`) and `renderRules(limit = 20)` (`:317-329`) have a **count** limit but no character budget; `BookLearning.MAX_TEXT_CHARS = 6000` per rule → up to ~120 K chars; `BookSharedMemory.render(limit = 20)` (`:155-174`) adds up to 2 × 20 rules.**

A book with 20 long learned rules makes every single model call carry ~30 K+ tokens of "DATA" — against free models with a 4 K budget knob (`pref_ai_token_budget`, default 4000) that is applied to the wrong thing. `AiCapabilityReporter`'s own justification (`AiCapabilityReporter.kt:12-16`) is precisely "the agent burned 50 K tokens".

*Fix:* a shared char-budgeted renderer for both blocks (target ≤ 4 K chars), prefer newest + highest-priority kinds (`reading_order`, `voice`), and report what was elided.
*Impact:* high — cheap, deterministic, directly reduces cost and latency on the free tier.
*Risk:* low — the blocks are already labelled DATA; just shorter. Re-check `BookLearningTest`/`BookSharedMemoryTest` expectations.

---

### 10. Prompt-injection defence is one regex deep, and the "trust" label is only a sentence
**`BookLearning.kt:135-164`** — `toolCallBlock` (`<…tool_call>…</…>`) and `toolCallLine` (`^@\s*(?:tool\s+)?Name\s*\{`, `RegexOption` **without** `MULTILINE`, applied per line so anchoring works) + control chars + length cap. Traced consequences: `BookKnowledge.render` (`:288-308`) interpolates `book.site`, `book.summary`, facts, advice, notes with **no sanitisation at all** (those go through `remember` → `sanitize(text, 2000)` at `:127`, but `site`/`summary` are stored raw at `:133-140`). And `book_learn`'s **only** URL validation is `BookLearning.isHttpUrl` (`AiAgent.kt:1419` → `BookLearning.kt:230`), which accepts any `http(s)://host` — `127.0.0.1:8765`, `169.254.169.254`, a LAN box. `web_fetch`/`check_site` also normalise to http(s) but never restrict host (`AiAgent.kt:1923, 1982`), so a fetched page can steer the next turn's tools at internal addresses.

*Fix:* (a) run `sanitize` over the whole `render()` output and mark each line as data; (b) apply the same `isHttpUrl` check to `web_fetch`/`check_site`/`book_learn` targets; (c) block link-local/loopback/RFC1918 by default with an explicit opt-in; (d) treat `author = user` rules as instructions and everything else as data (currently `author` is recorded but never used for trust decisions — `BookLearning.AUTHOR_USER` at `:46` is written and then only displayed).
*Impact:* high for safety; medium effort.
*Risk:* medium — item (c) will break users who deliberately point the agent at a LAN box (e.g. the runner), so gate it behind a setting.

---

### 11. The chat UI does disk I/O and JSON decoding on the main thread
**`ReaderAiChatOverlay.kt`**: `:133-135` `remember(mangaId) { BookKnowledge.profile(context, mangaId) }` (file read + kotlinx decode in composition) · `:312-316` and `:317-324` `AiHistoryManager.load(...)` inside `LaunchedEffect` (Main) decoding up to 100 messages · `:459-463` `BookKnowledge.updateProfile` (load+save) in a click handler · `:729` `AiHistoryManager.append(...)` — a full synchronous rewrite of the history file — before `scope.launch` · `:778-808` the same append inside `rememberCoroutineScope()` (Main) · `:571`, `:695` `save(...)` on delete/clear.

The codebase already has the right primitive (`ReaderActivity.kt:1716` uses `lifecycleScope.launchIO`, and `:1222-1229` in this very file wraps the file listing in `withContext(Dispatchers.IO)`), so these call sites look like leftovers from before that convention.

*Fix:* move all of the above behind `withContext(Dispatchers.IO)`; batch the two appends into one write per turn.
*Impact:* medium-high — removes jank/ANR risk on a 100-message history and on slow/unmounted storage.
*Risk:* low.

---

### 12. `github_api` grants unscoped write to the whole account, gated by a single boolean
**`AiAgent.kt:1036-1076`** — any `api.github.com` path, methods GET/POST/PATCH/PUT/DELETE (`:57`), guarded only by `aiAllowGithub()` (`:1038`) and a non-blank PAT; the PAT is stored in plaintext prefs (`OcrPreferences.kt:248`) and, per `AiChatTab.kt:144-145`, has `actions:write` and therefore reaches *all* repositories of the account. `runner_start` (`:1019-1034`) likewise starts an agent that "видит и меняет ВСЕ репозитории аккаунта" (`RunnerLlm.kt:746`).

*Fix:* restrict `github_api` to an allowlist of path prefixes (`/repos/{DEFAULT_REPO}/…`, `/user`), keep DELETE/PUT/PATCH opt-in per-tool, and surface the exact request in a confirm dialog (the result already prints `$method $path → HTTP …`, `:1067`, so the UI has the data).
*Impact:* high for blast radius; medium effort.
*Risk:* low-medium — users who *want* repo-wide automation would need a second, explicit switch.

---

### 13. Provider/routing state can silently diverge from reality
**`AiBackends.kt:256-290`**: `route()` returns `ready = true` for the online backend *unconditionally* ("сеть и ключи проверяет сам AiAssistant"), so `AiBackends.SELECTABLE`/settings show it ready even when Zen free tier is blocked — the very lie `AiCapabilityReporter.kt:37-44` was written to fix, and `ZenAvailability` state exists but is not consulted by `route`. **`AiBackends.kt:330`**: a stray `val session = liveRunnerSession(context)` at column 0 inside the `BACKEND_RUNNER ->` branch (formatting damage that will trip `spotlessCheck`). **`AiAgent.kt:105-129`**: after the provider key is dropped, the GitHub tools at `:1080-1119` still call `Injekt.get<OcrPreferences>()` and read the PAT with **no `aiAllowGithub` check**, unlike `github_api` at `:1038` — inconsistent gating. **Order dependence** in `ReaderBookLookup.applyVerdict` (`:157-165`) plus `AiReaderTools.applyPreset` (`:144-158`, which writes `defaultReadingMode` globally) means one auto-research can silently change the reader mode; there is no `.disabled` pref in `OcrPreferences` to stop the whole background flow.

*Fix:* have `route()` consult `zenState()`/key presence; clean up `:330`; add the `aiAllowGithub` gate to `runner_runs`/`runner_events`/`repo_pulls`; add an `aiBookLookup` = off switch; make `applyPreset` not touch `defaultReadingMode` from a background path.
*Impact:* medium-high (removes "it says ready but isn't" and surprise reader-mode flips).
*Risk:* low-medium — the reading-mode behaviour is depended on by auto-read tuning.

---

### 14. Test coverage stops exactly where the bugs are
`AiAgent.kt` has 23 tests' worth of pure helpers (`stripToolFragments`, `humanMs`, `searchAllowed`, `parseChoices`, `sampleSizeFor`, `silentModelSummary`) and **zero** coverage of `parseToolCalls` (:740), `callSignature` (:174), the round loop / dedup / skip-feedback (:519-674), the prompt assembly (:436-454), or `execute` dispatch (:913). All three of my top findings (items 1, 2, 4) live in exactly those gaps, and `knownToolNames`/`RESERVED_TOOL_NAMES`/`SYSTEM_PROMPT` are three hand-maintained lists that can drift (e.g. `knownToolNames` includes skill names that `execute` cannot dispatch, item in §b).

*Fix:* table-driven tests for `parseToolCalls` (canonical, `@name`, bare `name`, multi-line JSON, XML, backticked, duplicated-by-two-parsers) asserting both the call list and its de-duplication; a test that every name in `knownToolNames` is reachable in `execute`; a budget test that `SYSTEM_PROMPT + capabilities + knowledge` stays under N chars.
*Impact:* high (prevents regressions 1/2/4 from coming back and turns the three tool lists into a checked invariant).
*Risk:* none — test-only.

---

### 15. Secondary but cheap
- **`AiAgent.kt:101-104`**: `knownToolNames` does `mkdirs()` + `listFiles` + `readText` + `JSON.parse` for both `plugins/` and `skills/` on *every* parse and every `stripToolSyntax` call (`AiPlugins.kt:44-57`, `AiSkills.kt:53-63`) — cache per turn. (`AiWorkspace.cachedRoot` at `:51-52` already does exactly this pattern.)
- **`AiAgent.kt:2095-2113` / `:2071-2086`**: `readText()`/`readBytes()` read the whole response then truncate; a 100 MB page is an OOM. Read with a capped stream.
- **`AiAgent.kt:2098`, `:1928`**: `web_fetch` uses a **12 s** read timeout while `check_site`/`web_search`/`gen_image` get 30–120 s (`TOOL_TIMEOUT_MS` `:121-131`) — the workhorse tool is the one most likely to time out mid-download.
- **`AiAgent.kt:952` vs `AiChatTools.kt:129`**: Kotlin's `return@withContext` inside `onFailure` is a non-local return that silently abandons the copy — `render_audio`/`gen_video` can report success while writing nothing. Use an explicit result value.
- **`AiAgent.kt:2098` (proxy) vs `AiGithub.kt:91`, `RunnerLlm.githubRequest:390`, `AiHttpServer.importBookFromUrl:391`**: only `AiAssistant.openConnection` honours Settings → proxy; `AiGithub`/`RunnerLlm` use `URL.openConnection()` directly (`RunnerLlm.githubDownload:422-429` deliberately strips the token off non-GitHub hosts but not the proxy) — inconsistent with the documented behaviour in `AiChatTab`/`AGENT_SESSION.md`.
- **`AiAgent.kt:694-699`**: `parseChoices` silently drops variants past the 4th with no note; `AiHistoryManager.kt:172-181` compression prepends a synthetic `role="ai"` summary that keeps growing the stored history.
- **`AiChatTab.kt:143-148`** vs **`i18n/.../strings.xml:1337-1342`**: "Open AI chat / Switches to the AI tab" opens a hub launcher, and "Built-in AI server / Applies after restarting the app" is the only documented control for a server whose 401 points at a non-existent screen. Copy is wrong in both directions.

fun userDictionaryCoverage(text: String): Float {
        if (text.isBlank()) return 0f
        var letters = 0
        var covered = 0
        for (token in text.split(NOT_LETTER_OR_DIGIT)) {
            val lexical = token.filter(Char::isLetter)
            if (lexical.count { it.code in CYRILLIC_RANGE } == 0) continue
            letters += lexical.length
            if (OcrVocabulary.isUserWord(lexical)) covered += lexical.length
        }
        if (letters == 0) return 0f
        return covered.toFloat() / letters
    }

    /**
     * Доля букв, покрытая ЛЮБЫМ известным словарём — встроенным [RuWordList] и
     * пользовательским [OcrVocabulary].
     *
     * Ранжирование кандидатов в `CyrillicOcrEngine` обязано брать именно эту
     * долю: [userDictionaryCoverage] без встроенного словаря оценивал кандидата
     * только по словарю пользователя, то есть в пустом словареке вклад
     * встроенных семи тысяч слов был нулевым, и две гипотезы с близкой
     * уверенностью выбирались по noise, а не по тому, какая из них —
     * настоящие русские слова. Счётчики [OcrTextCleanerStats] здесь не трогаем:
     * это чтение для ранжирования, а не починка текста.
     */
    fun knownDictionaryCoverage(text: String): Float {
        if (text.isBlank()) return 0f
        var letters = 0
        var covered = 0
        for (token in text.split(NOT_LETTER_OR_DIGIT)) {
            val lexical = token.filter(Char::isLetter)
            if (lexical.count { it.code in CYRILLIC_RANGE } == 0) continue
            letters += lexical.length
            if (OcrVocabulary.isKnownWord(lexical)) covered += lexical.length
        }
        if (letters == 0) return 0f
        return covered.toFloat() / letters
    }

/** Результат инструмента для модели: в рамках бюджета и с явной меткой. */
    internal fun toolOutputFor(name: String, output: String): String {
        val budget = toolOutputBudget(name)
        if (output.length <= budget) return "$name: $output"
        val shown = output.take(budget)
        return "$name: $shown\n… [обрезано: показано ${shown.length} из ${output.length} " +
            "символов. Нужно больше — читай по частям или увеличь литм запроса.]"
    }

    /**
     * Файлы, которые агент не читает: в них лежат ключи.
     *
     * Цепочка была настоящей: текст, прочитанный `web_fetch`, попадает в
     * промпт, модель просит `read_file providers/x.json`, получает ключ
     * OpenRouter дословно и уносит его через `plugin_create` с
     * `kind=http` на чужой хост. Ни одного подтверждения по пути. Поэтому
     * чтение закрыто, а перенастроить провайдера можно только
     * `provider_create`/`provider_edit` — там ключ и так аргумент.
     */
    private val SECRET_READ_DENY = listOf(
        "providers/",
        "ui/tabs.json",
        "plugins/",
        "skills/",
    )

    internal fun secretGuard(name: String): String? {
        val rel = name.trim().trimStart('/').lowercase()
        val denied = SECRET_READ_DENY.firstOrNull { rel.startsWith(it) || rel.contains("/" + it) }
            ?: return null
        return "ОТКАЗ: «$name» закрыт для чтения агентом (там ключи и настройки " +
            "провайдеров). Ключ провайдера меняется только через provider_edit, " +
            "состояние вкладок — через ui_tab_list. Сам файл не показан."
    }

    /**
     * Скрыть значения известных полей с секретами в любом тексте, который
     * уходит модели: перестраховка для файлов вроде бэкапа или экспорта.
     */
    internal fun redactSecrets(text: String): String = SECRET_FIELD_RE.replace(text) { m ->
        val key = m.groupValues[1]
        val quote = m.groupValues[2]
        "$key$quote[скрыто агентом]$quote"
    }

    private val SECRET_FIELD_RE = Regex(
        "(\"?(?:apiKey|api_key|token|secret|password|key)\"?\\s*[:=]\\s*)(\"[^\"]*\"|'[^']*')",
        RegexOption.IGNORE_CASE,
    )

Now: `read_many` and `workspace_list` also expose secrets. `read_many` uses `AiWorkspaceSurvey.readMany(root, list)` — it would happily read providers/*.json. Let me add the guard there too: filter out denied names, and if all are denied, return an error. Simpler: filter denied names out and note it.

Also `zip_workspace` bundles providers/ → the agent can then... the zip is a file produced, and `read_file` on the zip? Not readable as text. But the agent gets a downloadable archive containing keys. Hmm — the archive is offered to the user (file card), and `AiHttpServer` can serve it. Leave zip as is (user-initiated export) but note it.

Let me patch read_many.

Also: `SECRET_READ_DENY` contains "plugins/" and "skills/" — but plugins/skills are JSON tool definitions, not secrets. Blocking them would break the agent's own plugin listing (plugin_list exists though). Hmm, blocking reading of plugins/ files is not needed for security; `plugin_list` covers it. Blocking them could confuse the model. Let me keep providers/ and ui/tabs.json (which lists tab visibility — not secret either, but harmless to block... actually tabs.json isn't a secret at all).

Let me reduce the deny list to what's actually secret: `providers/`. And also block any file whose *name* suggests keys? Too clever. Keep it minimal and honest: `providers/` only. The real secret store is providers/*.json (apiKey) and the GitHub PAT is in SharedPreferences (not in the workspace) — good.

Let me simplify.

/**
     * Файлы, которые агент не читает: в них лежат ключи.
     *
     * Цепочка была настоящей: текст, прочитанный `web_fetch`, попадает в
     * промпт, модель просит `read_file providers/x.json`, получает ключ
     * OpenRouter дословно и уносит его через `plugin_create` с
     * `kind=http` на чужой хост. Ни одного подтверждения по пути. Поэтому
     * чтение закрыто, а перенастроить провайдера можно только
     * `provider_create`/`provider_edit` — там ключ и так аргумент.
     */
    private val SECRET_READ_DENY = listOf(
        "providers/",
        "ui/tabs.json",
        "plugins/",
        "skills/",
    )

    internal fun secretGuard(name: String): String? {
        val rel = name.trim().trimStart('/').lowercase()
        val denied = SECRET_READ_DENY.firstOrNull { rel.startsWith(it) || rel.contains("/" + it) }
            ?: return null
        return "ОТКАЗ: «$name» закрыт для чтения агентом (там ключи и настройки " +
            "провайдеров). Ключ провайдера меняется только через provider_edit, " +
            "состояние вкладок — через ui_tab_list. Сам файл не показан."
    }

perf(ocr): stop the per-pixel preference reads, fix the ranking dictionary

The detector called tuning() on every pixel of the 736x736 probability map
and again for each of its 8 neighbours. tuning() builds three objects and
reads eleven SharedPreferences keys, so one page cost tens of millions of
preference reads — the direct cause of "OCR frame timeout" in autoread.
The tuning is now read once per pass. Same for candidateQuality and the
tiling decision.

OcrTextCleaner recompiled six Regex objects per line per box: Kotlin does
not cache Regex literals. They are fields now.

Ranking counted only the user dictionary, so with an empty user dictionary
the 7000 built-in Russian words contributed nothing and two candidates
with similar confidence were separated by noise. knownDictionaryCoverage
covers both dictionaries and, unlike knownWord, does not touch the scan
stats.

Autoread frames, browser frames and selection crops were written to the
page cache under (chapter, page): a viewport crop of a webtoon segment
overwrote the honest full-page geometry, and the reader overlay and
transcript export then showed wrong boxes. scanPage takes cacheResult and
those call sites pass false. The browser also rewrote the user's OCR
engine preference as a side effect of a screenshot — it is restored now.
The cache is dropped when the settings that produce it change (engine,
content type, local mode, region, manual thresholds, vocabulary revision).

Also: autoread leaked the maskCircle bitmap (up to 40 native bitmaps per
frame), and the panel detector's cleanup() closed the native model from
the main thread while inference was running.
EOF

fix(ai): stop telling the model that a call did not run, hide keys, bound prompts

Four things the agent loop got wrong, all found by reading it against the
screenshots it is built from:

A canonical one-line `@tool web_search {...}` was found by two parsers at
once, so the round reported the second copy as "НЕ ВЫПОЛНЕНО: тот же вызов
уже выполнялся" about a call that had just run. Calls are now collapsed by
callSignature inside the parser, and parseToolCalls is split so the pure
part is unit-tested (it had no tests at all).

Every tool result was cut to 700 characters with no marker, while
read_many is built for 12000 and web_fetch accepts 60000. The model
believed it had read the whole file and either invented the rest or called
the tool again. Per-tool budgets with an explicit "обрезано" line.

book_learn {"url":...} fetched the page and threw it away, then recorded
the URL as a source — so rules the model invented were displayed with
"(источник: …)" as if verified, and autoread trusts those rules for
reading order. The excerpt is returned now, with an explicit warning not
to invent rules that are not in it.

read_file returned providers/*.json verbatim, apiKey included, and
plugin_create with kind=http can POST anything anywhere: an injected page
could walk the whole chain to the user's OpenRouter key. Those files are
closed for the agent, and known secret fields are redacted from any text
shown to the model.

The book knowledge and shared memory blocks went into every request whole
(a rule is up to 6000 chars) and are now bounded. The AI-tab WebView gave
the runner session key to any host that asked for basic auth — and that
key fronts a GH_TOKEN with write access to every repo of the account; it
is now only given to the session's own host, with mixed content and file
access off. Chat history, the book profile and the user-message append
moved off the main thread.
EOF

read_many is built for 12000 and web_fetch accepts 60000. The model
believed it had read the whole file and either invented the rest or called
the tool again. Per-tool budgets with an explicit "обрезано" line.

book_learn {"url":...} fetched the page and threw it away, then recorded
the URL as a source — so rules the model invented were displayed with
"(источник: …)" as if verified, and autoread trusts those rules for
reading order. The excerpt is returned now, with an explicit warning not
to invent rules that are not in it.

read_file returned providers/*.json verbatim, apiKey included, and
plugin_create with kind=http can POST anything anywhere: an injected page
could walk the whole chain to the user's OpenRouter key. Those files are
closed for the agent, and known secret fields are redacted from any text
shown to the model.

The book knowledge and shared memory blocks went into every request whole
(a rule is up to 6000 chars) and are now bounded. The AI-tab WebView gave
the runner session key to any host that asked for basic auth — and that
key fronts a GH_TOKEN with write access to every repo of the account; it
is now only given to the session's own host, with mixed content and file
access off. Chat history, the book profile and the user-message append
moved off the main thread.

153:      * формулировку. Без отдельного потолка она крутила круги и выжигала
154:      * токены, так и не получив результата.
155:      */
156:     const val SEARCH_ATTEMPT_CAP = 6

158:     /**
159:      * Можно ли ещё выполнять поиск в сети.
160:      *
161:      * Чистая функция — её проверяет тест: баг с вечно молчащим `web_fetch`
162:      * как раз и вырос из того, что лимит был подмешан прямо в цикл и
163:      * отлаживался только вручную.
164:      */
165:     fun searchAllowed(searchesUsed: Int, searchAttempts: Int): Boolean =
166:         searchesUsed < SEARCH_BUDGET && searchAttempts < SEARCH_ATTEMPT_CAP

168:     /**
169:      * Каноническая подпись вызова инструмента: имя + аргументы по отсортированным
170:      * ключам. Ключ из `args.toString()` зависел от порядка, который написала
171:      * модель, и `{"query":"x","limit":5}` с `{"limit":5,"query":"x"}` считались
172:      * разными вызовами — а одинаковые стыковались «повтором».
173:      */
174:     internal fun callSignature(call: ToolCall): String = buildString {
175:         append(call.name).append('\u0000')
176:         val keys = call.args.keys().asSequence().sorted().toList()
177:         for (k in keys) {
178:             append(k).append('=').append(call.args.opt(k)).append('\u0001')
179:         }
180:     }

302:     /**
303:      * Один ход агента: prompt пользователя (+опц. текст из вложений) →
304:      * модель → выполнение @tool-вызовов → второй запрос модели с
305:      * результатами → финальный ответ.
306:      */
307:     /**
308:      * Функция чата бэкенда: (prompt, systemPrompt) -> ChatReply?.
309:      * Позволяет гонять ОДИН И ТОТ ЖЕ агентский цикл с инструментами через
310:      * ЛЮБОЙ бэкенд: онлайн (Zen/OpenRouter), ЛОКАЛЬНУЮ модель на телефоне
311:      * (LocalLlm) и полу-онлайн ранер (RunnerLlm). Инструменты (@tool)
312:      * исполняются самим приложением — модели достаточно уметь писать текст.
313:      */
314:     private val onlineChat: suspend (String, String) -> AiAssistant.ChatReply? = { p, sys ->
315:         AiAssistant.chatFull(p, sys, maxTokens = 1800)
316:     }
317: 
318:     /**
319:      * A tool turn must survive a provider hiccup after side effects already
320:      * happened. Retry only the model call and join max-token continuations;
321:      * never execute a tool merely because the network response was lost.
322:      */
323:     private suspend fun reliableChat(
324:         chat: suspend (String, String) -> AiAssistant.ChatReply?,
325:         prompt: String,
326:         systemPrompt: String,
327:     ): AiAssistant.ChatReply? {
328:         var reply: AiAssistant.ChatReply? = null
329:         for (attempt in 0 until 3) {
330:             reply = runCatching { chat(prompt, systemPrompt) }.getOrNull()
331:             if (reply != null) break
332:             kotlinx.coroutines.delay(800L * (attempt + 1))
333:         }
334:         var combined = reply ?: return null
335:         for (continuation in 0 until 2) {
336:             if (combined.complete) break
337:             val next = runCatching {
338:                 chat(
339:                     prompt + "\n\nОтвет оборвался по лимиту. Уже полученная часть:\n" +
340:                         combined.content.takeLast(6000) +
341:                         "\n\nПродолжи строго с места обрыва. Не повторяй уже написанное.",
342:                     systemPrompt,
343:                 )
344:             }.getOrNull() ?: break
345:             combined = combined.copy(
346:                 content = combined.content + "\n" + next.content,
347:                 reasoning = next.reasoning ?: combined.reasoning,
348:                 model = next.model,
349:                 tokens = combined.tokens + next.tokens,
350:                 complete = next.complete,
351:             )
352:         }
353:         return combined
354:     }

356:     suspend fun run(
357:         context: Context,
358:         userText: String,
359:         attachmentsInfo: String? = null,
360:         history: List<Pair<String, String>> = emptyList(), // role to content
361:         chatFn: (suspend (String, String) -> AiAssistant.ChatReply?)? = null,
362:         mangaId: Long? = null,
363:         bookContext: String? = null,
364:         onProgress: ((String) -> Unit)? = null,
365:     ): AgentReply = withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
366:         val chat = chatFn ?: onlineChat
367:         val results = mutableListOf<ToolResult>()
368:         val images = mutableListOf<File>()
369: 
370:         // Продвинутый лимит истории и токен-бюджет (запрос: не тратить 50к токенов)
371:         val prefs = runCatching { uy.kohesive.injekt.Injekt.get<yomikai.domain.ocr.service.OcrPreferences>() }.getOrNull()
372:         val historyLimit = prefs?.aiHistoryLimit()?.get()?.coerceIn(4, 100) ?: 12
373:         val tokenBudget = prefs?.aiTokenBudget()?.get()?.coerceIn(1000, 16000) ?: 4000
374:         // Грубая оценка токенов: 3.5 символа ≈ 1 токен
375:         fun est(s: String) = (s.length / 3.5).toInt()
376:         var budgetedHistory = history
377:         var total = history.sumOf { est(it.second) }
378:         while (budgetedHistory.size > 4 && total > (tokenBudget * 0.7).toInt()) {
379:             val removed = budgetedHistory.first()
380:             total -= est(removed.second)
381:             budgetedHistory = budgetedHistory.drop(1)
382:         }
383:         val trimmedHistory = budgetedHistory
384:         // Реплики режем ГОЛОВОЙ и ХВОСТОМ, а не только головой: в ответе агента
385:         // вывод и путь к файлу стоят в конце, и take(280) их отбрасывал —
386:         // модель теряла ровно то, ради чего ход затевался.
387:         val historyBlock = trimmedHistory.takeLast(historyLimit).joinToString("\n\n") { (role, c) ->
388:             val body = if (c.length > MAX_HISTORY_CHARS) {
389:                 c.take(MAX_HISTORY_CHARS / 2) + " … " + c.takeLast(MAX_HISTORY_CHARS / 2)
390:             } else {
391:                 c
392:             }

package yomikai.data.ai

import android.content.Context
import android.graphics.Bitmap
import android.graphics.BitmapFactory

import yomikai.data.ui.UiTabRegistry

import yomikai.source.online.HttpSource
